chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I partner with the non-Muslim (Al-Ilj) such that the land, the seed, and the oxen are from me, and the oversight, irrigation, and labor in the crop until it becomes wheat and barley are upon the non-Muslim. Then the distribution occurs, so the Sultan takes his right, and what remains remains on the stipulation that for the non-Muslim is one-third of it, and for me is the remainder.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with that.' I said, 'So would it be for me if he were to return to me from what the land produced the seed, and the remainder be divided?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Rather, you partnered with him on the stipulation that the seed is from you, and upon him is the irrigation and the oversight.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on agricultural partnership between a Muslim and a non-Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of agricultural partnership (musharakah) between a Muslim and a Zimmi, emphasizing that the Imam’s clarification distinguishes between capital contribution (seed) and operational labor (irrigation/care). It highlights the Shia legal principle that profit-sharing agreements are valid as long as the nature of contributions is clearly defined, reflecting the flexibility of Islamic commercial law in practical economic contexts.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I associated with Al Ilj (the non-Muslim) so there happened to be from me, the land, and the sowing, and the oxen, and there happened to be upon Al Ilj (non-Muslim) the overseeing, and the irrigation, and the workers in the farming until there came to be wheat and barley, and there happened to be the distribution, so the Sultan (ruling authority) took his right (taxation), and there remained what remained upon a stipulation that for Al Ilj (the non-Muslim) from it would be the third, and for me would be the remainder’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with that’. I said, ‘So would it be for me if he was to return to me from what I had brought out of the seeds, and the remainder to be divided?’ Heasws said: ‘But rather, you participated with him upon a stipulation that the sowing would be from you, and upon him would be the irrigation and the overseeing’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhiy who has narrated the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I become a partner of an al-‘ilj (a great non-Muslim person). I provide land, seed, and the bull. Al-‘ilj does the plantation and other works for the farm. When the wheat or barely comes, the produce is divided; al-Sultan takes away his right, one-third is for al-‘ilj and the remaining is for me. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’

I then asked if the seed can be given to me from the produce of the land and the rest is divided. He (the Imam) said, ‘You have formed a partnership which required you to provide the seed and he must provide water and other works.’”
